reason: Seeing the curve above the line between O and P shows why the limit is 16 and why we integrate curve minus line.

scenes.title: Why the area is curve minus line, from 0 to 16
scenes.purpose: See where C and l meet, that C lies above l between O and P, and that the area grows to 256/3 at x = 16.

steps.text: The curve and line cross at $O$ and at $P$. Setting $8\sqrt{x} - x = x$ gives $\sqrt{x} = 4$, so $x = 16$, not $4$. This is the M1 for finding the non-zero $x$-coordinate of $P$.

Drag $Q$ along $C$ between $O$ and $P$. Its $y$-value is always bigger than the line's $y$-value, so the height of the region is curve $-$ line $= 8x^{\frac{1}{2}} - 2x$. Reversing this gives a negative area.

Write $\sqrt{x}$ as $x^{\frac{1}{2}}$ and integrate: $\int (8x^{\frac{1}{2}} - 2x)\,\mathrm{d}x = \frac{16}{3}x^{\frac{3}{2}} - x^2$. The shaded area up to $k$ is this expression evaluated at $k$. This earns the integration M1 and the A1.

Drag $k$ to $16$: the region closes at $P$. The working $\frac{1024}{3} - \frac{768}{3}$ gives the area $\frac{256}{3} \approx 85.3$, matching the label. This is the M1 for the limits and the final A1.

guide.what_you_see: The curve $C$ ($y=8\sqrt{x}-x$) and the line $l$ ($y=x$) from the question, meeting at $O$ and at $P(16,16)$. The shaded region is the part of $R$ from $x=0$ up to the slider value $k$, and it fills all of $R$ when $k=16$.

legend.meaning: The curve $y=8\sqrt{x}-x$ for $x\geqslant 0$ from the question.
The origin $(0,0)$, the first point where $C$ and $l$ meet.
The second meeting point $(16,16)$, found from $8\sqrt{x}-x=x$, which gives $\sqrt{x}=4$.
The region between $C$ and $l$ from $x=0$ to $x=k$. Its area is $\int_0^k (8x^{\frac12}-2x)\,\mathrm{d}x$, and at $k=16$ it is the whole region $R$ of the question.
A point you can drag along $C$, used to compare the curve's height with the line's height at the same $x$.
The vertical grey line at $x=k$, marking the right-hand edge of the shaded region.

interact.do: Drag the slider from $1$ up to $16$ (it starts at $6$) to move the right-hand edge of the shaded region.
interact.watch: The shading grows and the 'Area from 0 to $k$' reading rises. It is about $42.4$ at $k=6$ and about $68.7$ at $k=10$. At $k=16$ the region closes at $P$ and the reading is $\frac{256}{3}\approx 85.3$.

interact.do: Drag $Q$ along $C$ between $O$ and $P$, that is for $x$ from $0$ to $16$.
interact.watch: The curve's $y$-value at $Q$ stays above the line's $y$-value for every $x$ between $0$ and $16$. For example, at $x=4$ they are $12$ and $4$. That is why the height of the region is curve minus line, $8x^{\frac12}-2x$.

question_link.text: $O$ and $P$ are the meeting points of $C$ and $l$, and $P$ at $x=16$ is the result of the first M1. The shaded region is $R$, and its area is the integral of curve minus line, $\frac{16}{3}x^{\frac32}-x^2$. That integral earns the integration M1 and the A1. Substituting the limits $16$ and $0$ gives the final M1, and the reading at $k=16$ is the final A1 value $\frac{256}{3}$.

read_off: 'Area from 0 to $k$' is the area of the shaded region, equal to $\frac{16}{3}k^{\frac32}-k^2$. It reaches the exact area $\frac{256}{3}\approx 85.3$ of $R$ when $k=16$.

'At Q: curve $y$ = ..., line $y$ = ...' gives the height of $C$ at $Q$ and the height of $l$ at the same $x$. The first number is always larger between $O$ and $P$, and their difference is the height of the strip, $8\sqrt{x}-2x$.
